utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon to everyone. Mr. Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Good afternoon to everyone in the courtroom. This is case number IT-06-90-T, the Prosecutor versus Ante Gotovina, et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Before we continue with the witness, Mr. Misetic, the Chamber would like to deal with a few procedural matters. Witness AG-20 was subpoenaed for the 5th of June, but we have no indication yet whether the subpoena has been served and whether the witness will come, because there may be other problems as well. Is there any other witness for Friday to replace him?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Unfortunately, Mr. President, the witness who is scheduled for Monday could not change his plans to come earlier.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Of course, if we look at the history of -- of the subpoena of witness AG-20 then we see that here and there, there are some delays. Chamber tried to do its utmost best. But the first motion was filed I think on 7th of May, and then it took a while to get it complete. Because when it was complete on the 21st, the Chamber immediately drafted the decision and intended to file it on the 22nd, but then due to some practicalities in relation to the filing, it was finally the attempt to have it electronically filed on the 21st failed and that means that the final was effective on the 25th. But a lot of time was lost in the beginning, and this might cause the type of delays we are looking at now, and the Chamber may also not have been accurate in every respect, filing on the 22nd failed. I don't know whether a lot could have been done over that weekend. But, nevertheless, our filing should have been perfect on that 22nd as well. But now we are facing possible delays. We have to try at any cost to avoid that gaps will exist. For next week, there may be other uncertainties as well. Witnesses AG-61.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: That is correct --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... This will be another witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: That is correct. We have two witnesses both claiming health problem, Mr. President. We are in the process of trying to confirm. I have received a message as to how to proceed with one of the witnesses which I will do tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: With respect to the other witness, we are waiting for information from VWU so that we can it on to the Trial Chamber to make an assessment as to whether a subpoena should be issued.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: If not, in speaking to that witness, we would file an immediate request for a videolink because he was willing to testify via videolink and depending on how fast the Registry can set that up, we would obviously proceed as fast as the Registry can get it done.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Perhaps if there's any chance that you would need a videolink, try to get in touch with the Registry at the earliest possibility because they will be able to tell you exactly what is needed. Also, of course, depends on from where the videolink needs to be --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: One thought that has come to my mind, and I will discusses it with my colleagues on behalf of the Prosecution during the break, is the possibility given the anticipated length of time I think it may take to get the witness's medical records in order. If the witness has no objection to testifying via videolink to see whether the parties might agree to that process just so we can maintain our schedule, but I will discuss that with the Prosecution, and then obviously we'll consult with the Chamber and see what the Chamber thinks about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yeah. And although it might not be easy, it -- it's always good to have some replacement which can quickly move available. I do see that that is not always easy. We really have to try to avoid any loss of time in court. Mr. Mikulicic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I would like to report technical difficulties. We have no B/C/S translation on the channel 5. There is kind of mixed up French and B/C/S translation. So the accused cannot follow the procedure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The advantage is they're not speaking B/C/S and French at the same time. But I also just noticed that we first get some translation into B/C/S and then we get some translation in French. I see this gesture in the booth, meaning, I don't know how to resolve it. Let's see. It looks very much as if the technicians are ...

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: It seems to be all right now, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's all right now. Then I don't know who did it, but thanks for fixing it. Next item is we received filing of the Gotovina Defence's motion to add two witness-related documents to its 65 ter list. When could we expect a response from the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: We can do it right now. We have no objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No objections. No objections from any of the other Defence teams? It doesn't seem that my question has the full attention of the Cermak Defence but ...

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I'm told no objection. I'm sorry, Your Honour. We were just -- [Microphone not activated] -- technical matter between us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I see that. It's good to know, Mr. Kay, that if you're told that there are no objections that that's what follows. That's -- now the next question will be, who is telling you what to say. Must be Ms. Higgins in this case. Then the request is granted to add the two witness-related documents to the 65 ter list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber, as I said yesterday, has received a copy of the non-disclosure agreement, which I do understand is an agreement between all parties; that is, including all Defence teams. We earlier said that we would have a look at the matter and that it was most likely that the parties would file the agreement so that it would be on the record. The Chamber has meanwhile looked at the agreement and accepts the agreement. I add to this, that, in earlier decisions, sometimes we find an obligation to keep a log of to whom material is disclosed and when under one of the exceptions. We do not find any agreement on that. And it might be a wise thing to consider that it does not in any way invalidate the agreement as reached, but it might, for the future, it might avoid any discussions at a later stage, if such a log would be kept, and, of course, I'm now mainly looking at the Prosecution. So the Chamber accepts the agreement reached, suggests to the parties to see whether it would be good to have an additional clause on keeping a log on to whom material is disclosed. Therefore, the parties are invited to file the agreement so that it's on the record. And I further inform you that the interim decision on Defence requests to -- for order of non-disclosure for materials disclosed to the Prosecution and co-defendants is not applicable because replaced by the present agreement, which will be filed by the parties. Any questions in relation to this? Then the last issue is that on the 27th of May, there was a reference in court in relation to the talks between you, Mr. Kehoe, and Mr. Russo about expert reports. And I think you asked whether it would be okay if it would be reported early this week to the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We are in the midst of this week.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes. And I had a discussion initially with Mr. Russo and with counsel about the dates and turning those over and the bulk of those reports with -- discussed with Mr. Waespi will be turned over in two weeks. And I do believe he found that satisfactory, which will give the requisite period of time for the Prosecution to deal with those reports.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Waespi, you're in a position to confirm that, I take it?

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So an agreement has been reached on the matter. Mr. Waespi, you're the receiving party in this respect. If there would be any problem, I think it would be incumbent upon you to inform the Chamber that there are problems, but we do not expect anything in view of the agreement you have reached with Mr. Kehoe. I've got no further procedural matters on my list. If there are none, then, I would like to ask Madam Usher to escort Mr. Lazarevic into the courtroom. Could I meanwhile, to the extent it is possible to make an assessment at this moment, already inquire with the parties how much time they would need for cross-examination or, as far as Defence is concerned, let's say examination of Mr. Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: We have nothing, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Nothing. Mr. Mikulicic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Probably nothing, Your Honour. If something, that will be five to ten minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. It's hard to estimate it, but definitely we will be done today. I would say maybe two hours, but that could vary significantly based on the witness's responses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I can imagine that. Which also means that there is a possibility that we could start with the next witness already today. So there's no reason yet to --

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: We had discussed the matter with Mr. Kehoe, and he is aware of that situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, we have discussed, and I talked to Mr. Hedaraly, we have the next witness who will be in the room after the first break as opposed to having them sitting here all day, so ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lazarevic, I would like to remind that the solemn declaration that you gave yesterday at the beginning of your testimony still binds you. That means that also today you are under an obligation to tell the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth. Mr. Misetic will now continue his examination-in-chief. Mr. Misetic, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Let me right at the outset remind you of the ground rules again. Both you and I, for the benefit of the interpreters and the court reporter really need to slow our pace down and really need to enunciate when we speak. So if I give you some hand signals sometimes, I'm not trying to be rude just to remind you to help us with the court staff here.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Yesterday we left off with what happened after you arrived in Serbia. And I would like to pick up there. Can you tell us a little bit what happened -- you talk about being arrested in Serbia. Can you describe the day you were arrested, what happened and what events transpired?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It happened very, very fast after my arrival. Within two days police arrived, regular police and asked me to come with them and go to the station in the city, police station. I asked him why, said we don't know, but they will tell you when you get there. I did get there, and I had all my documents with me, which I presented there, and I think there was a gentleman from DB in the corner in the office.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: DB meaning?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Drzavna Bezbednosti [phoen].

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Which is?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Secret police.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He looked at the papers, and gave a little note to the station commander that said, Well, we don't really need this guy; he's not from over there. So they let me.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: When you say, "he's not from over there ..."

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Obviously he meant from RSK.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And what happened next?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They released me. So I went home the same afternoon. Next morning they came back again, but instead of taking me to this place where I was, the day before they took me to another place and I stayed there, even though I argued the same reason why I shouldn't be taken in. Now, they couldn't care less, so I was placed on a bus with the rest of the people from Krajina were there. It was like a gathering centre, I guess. Approximately 2.000 of us there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: The 2.000, what -- can you describe the 2.000?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 2.000, I can only assume that all 2.000 were the people who actually were refugees from the RSK.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Was it all men? Mixture of men and women?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, men only.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. In the Milosevic case you described at page 12469, a huge convoy of buses. Can you tell us how many buses there were?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On that particular afternoon when we left, there were 12 buses.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 12 buses. No standing room. Everybody had their own seats, but there were four police officers in escort on the bus.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And where did the bus take you?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We had no idea until we actually arrived there. They never stopped anywhere in between. They never offered any explanation where are we going. And once it was dark, we saw little signs saying Dalj, then we realized where we were going.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Dalj being spelled?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: D-a-l-j.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And where is Dalj?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Eastern Slavonia.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us -- give us an approximation of the date we're talking about?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I arrived home around 10th, should be around 12th of August.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And when you arrived Dalj, what happened next?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We arrived there and it was total darkness. There were a lot of shouting going on outside, fall out, fall out, fall out. As I was coming off the bus - I was kind in the middle of bus - as I was coming off the bus, somebody pulled me aside and said, Well, you're not there; you come with me. And I couldn't even see in the dark who it was, but I coudl see in front of me that people are being taken through a cauldron, like, you know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Through a ... ?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: How do I explain this. When you have people lined up on either side and you're supposed to run in between, but they're very close to you and to themselves, like at arm length.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Like a gauntlet?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Gauntlet. That's what I was try to say. I said cauldron which is kind of witchcraft. Anyway, sorry about that. I mean gauntlet. And they were really beaten as they were pushed through. There were people there with batons.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: With?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Batons.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Baton, okay.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah. The gentleman who took me aside, took me straight to the building. Once we were in the building I could see who it was. It was one of the young Arkan's guys that I knew from Krajina. Apparently he knew that I was not born over there, that I was born in Belgrade, so I think he prevented from anything bad happening to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. What was the -- what was the place that you arrived at?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was like a huge camp, a military camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: What was the purpose of the camp?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did find that out about two days later. They are the masters in the morning with lined up everybody in the yard, there was a lot of shouting going on, a lot of verbal abuse, a lot of physical abuse by the people running the camp, they were all Tigers, according to their badges belonging to this infamous unit of Arkan. So when I talked to some of the officers of this camp, they told me they were there to be retrained and sent back to Croatia to fight.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Approximately, if you can tell us, first, how long were you in this camp?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Four to five days. I think on the fifth day they came and picked me up and took me out.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Do you know how long this camp was in existence?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Do you know how many men, roughly, were processed through this camp?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My estimate of what I have seen, the buses coming in mornings and evenings, anything between 6 to 8.000 men.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, I would like to play a short video and ask, based on your answers here, whether some of the experiences described herein are consistent with what you have just testified about, in terms of your experiences. Mr. Registrar, this is 1D1634.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There may be a problem. I now hear French translation which will then be processed into a French transcript. We have -- I read the English, but it is not spoken English, which means that the English transcript will be incomplete. One has to look at the video to see what was said during this video-clip. Is there any way that we get complete transcript which means that the English booth would, of course, verify whether the English translation we see is correct or at least to -- to translate the text spoken so that we have a full English and a full French transcript? Is that possible? Then I would like to --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Your Honour, normally the practice was that the interpreters received a written transcript in the booths which was the reason why the English booth did not read the text from the screen since we did not receive a hard copy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You're perfectly right, that is the -- and I see from here that someone now hands out a transcript. If the parties could always take care that booths are provided with hard copies of the transcripts.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: We have a copy now. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You're perfectly right. I don't know where it got stuck. Apparently it was nearby. So it must have been close. Let's re-start so that we have a full transcript, although perhaps the French twice. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Can we just confirm that the French booth has the transcript? It does, okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Let's start again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: "THE INTERPRETER: [Voiceover] "Narrator: In Eastern Slavonia Arkan made his fortune on selling scarce items on the black market, turning the area into his own private state. In mid 1995, the police in Serbia arrested refugees and sent them to Arkan's camp in Erdut. "Milan: When I recall this I feel sick. The police arrested all of us that were in the reception centre, put us on buses. "Borislav Pelevic: It was a completely insane decision. People were practically kidnapped; they were practically abducted. "Dusan: When we arrived I didn't even know where I was going. When we arrived in Erdut ... "Milan: Heads were sticking out of the window, shaved heads, as we were -- as we arrived they filed us in line. "Dusan: When we handed all our documents and removed or clothes, they removed our watches, necklaces, everything. No one was allowed to keep anything, not a thing. "Borislav Pelevic: The police escorted them to the RSK police, and they assigned them to these recruitment centres. One of the centres was our centre in Erdut. They were treated with maximum correctness. "Dusan: These people were pushed in the manner that they were forced to bark like dogs. They had these small houses like kennels, people were chained to them, and they were forced to bark like dogs. "Milan: There was even first, I can say that people were being shot in the leg, and also thanks to ... they sometimes fall between themselves, and so they got him -- got to him. "Dusan: Arkan said to us, he spoke to us and said, Listen up. We all listened. Who wants to give me a blow-job? These were the words with which Mr. Arkan spoke to us. We all stood there, nobody dared ask anything, utter a single word."

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Stop. We'll stop the video right there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm just wondering whether ... of course, the last text on the screen is not included in, because I do not ... Could you have a look at the transcript, Mr. Misetic, and see whether --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- we have the full portion.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes. I believe that is complete, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Then please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Lazarevic, the camp in Erdut, is that the camp that you were at as well?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I assume. I am not quite certain I was in one camp. I remember seeing Dalj, but I don't remember seeing any other road signs.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But according to this, there were several of those, so ...

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: The treatment described in this video, is that consistent with what you witnessed when you arrived one of Arkan's camps after Operation Storm?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The gentleman with the hidden face?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There's a portion where the former general of Arkan is speaking to about being correctly treated; it is insane. It's a lie. The gentleman who described the situation at the beginning, he is absolutely correct. I went through that too.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, we tender the clip into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: We haven't seen the whole clip yet, it seems. So we have no objection to the portion that has been shown yet. But as to the portion we haven't seen, we obviously cannot express a portion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is there any portion which is not played but which you tender into evidence?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I will tender up to this point, and I guess we'll cut the the video from this point forward.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then appear to be no objections against the portion played. Can you please upload that limited portion because once that is done, the Chamber would admitted that evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, that would be number?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1469, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, could you please inform us as soon as it has been uploaded, the new version, either you, Mr. Misetic, or Mr. Registrar so that a final decision can be taken. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Lazarevic, are you familiar, or did you participate in any meetings where the International Committee of the Red Cross was present?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Quite a few, actually.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Did you have any experience in situations where Croats living in the Krajina wished to depart the Krajina and go into Croatian-held territory?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That happened too.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. In the process of Croats leaving the Krajina to go to Croatian-held territory, are you aware of the ICRC participating in some of those transfers?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were absolutely always a part of those exchanges. They were really exchanges, but not a case of, I would assume, three Croat nationals have expressed the wish to cross to the Croatian-held territory, we just let it go. It was always the case, if we give you three, you give us three. So in the instances when there was a multiple exchanges like that, Red Cross was always there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Do you know if, prior to their departure from the Krajina if Croats had to sign a form -- not had. If the Croats signed a form indicating the voluntariness of their departure?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In every of the instances, there was exchange of people like this. The members of the International Red Cross would take the people aside from the group and speak to them, like without us being -- Serbs being present there. What -- are they willingly going, or were they pushed or forces or whatever? And in the end they would given a documents to sign that they are willingly crossing.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Who gave them the document to sign?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Somebody from the Red Cross.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, have I no further questions. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Misetic. Perhaps I have one follow-up question, the last questions. These exchanges, as you said, what time-frame are we talking about?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Throughout the conflict.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Throughout the conflict, it is 1991 to 1995, not after Operation Storm?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not after, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If I just can clarify this. I was member of commission in the Sector North for exchange of people who are willing to go leave, exchange of soldiers who died in a battle on either side, they had to be exchanged as well. So I was kind of well familiar with the situation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could you tell us during that whole period of approximately four years, how many in total, how many persons alive or, as you said, sometime corpses of deceased persons would be involved in this type of exchanges?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Several hundred.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Several hundred.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have no questions of the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You have no questions. Mr. Mikulicic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: No questions as well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No questions from Mr. Mikulicic. Mr. Hedaraly, are you ready to cross-examine Mr. Lazarevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: I will be in a few seconds, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Lazarevic you will be cross-examined by Mr. Hedaraly. Mr. Hedaraly is counsel for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Your area of responsibility was the 21st Corps; is that right?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And your office was based in the command centre in Topusko.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: During your time with the ARSK, you never moved to a different command centre, did you?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The HQ itself did move, but my part of the office always remained within Topusko.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And you're a liaison officer for the 21st Corps; is that right?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And you did not have any demand function at the headquarters of the 21st Corps?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely none.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And I will as well try to pause between your answers and my question, and I will invite you to do the same, as Mr. Misetic did. And hopefully we'll get some help along the way. Now, can can you describe for the Court what was your area of responsibility, the area of the 21st Corps?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't quite understand what you ask me.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Geographically, what area did it encompass?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is approximately 70 kilometres long and around 20 kilometres wide. And goes from area of Slunj to Glina; that was the area of responsibility of the 21st Corps. Consequently, that was my area of responsibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And that is entirely within Sector North?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: So north of Gracac municipality? Gracac being in Lika?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah. That would be covered by Lika Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Okay. Because 21st Corps was a cordon corps; right?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Which was with a different part than Lika or Dalmatia which was the southern part of the Krajina?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Thanks. Now, your knowledge, everything that you have testified about today both in your statement and yesterday and today is based on your personal experiences and observations in that area; is that right?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And during Operation Storm, you were in Topusko; is that right?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Now you testified yesterday that during Operation Storm, you had your hands full with what was happening in Sector North.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Did you receive any information at that time about what was happening in Sector South?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only unconfirmed reports.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And what were these unconfirmed reports?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Knin is falling, army has withdrawn, the civilians leaving in mass, that kind of things. But not -- again, I have to stress this, not as an official report from the south.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: So you did not get any reports as to who was attacking where?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In detail I had only what was happening in Sector North.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Did you have any information as to, in Sector South, what units were defending which parts of the sector?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Unfortunately, no information.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Did you have any communication with anyone from Sector South on either the 4th or 5th of August?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After the 5th, no. No communication.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And before the 5th, did you have communications with anyone from Sector South?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I said before this date to that date, what I'm trying to say is before the attack, we had a regular communication on a daily basis. After the attack has commenced, nothing.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: So as soon as Operation Storm started, you did not -- you did not have any communication with anyone from Sector South; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My last communication with the HQ of Knin was when I sent them a telex about the pending attack the following morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Okay. We'll get to that in a few minutes. Now, there was some confusion yesterday and the Presiding Judge asked you to clarify certain of your responses that you gave regarding the Croatian flag flying over Knin castle, if you remember. And I was re-reading that exchange. And I just want to make sure that your testimony is as clear as possible. So, first you said that you saw this on the television, and you thought that this cannot be, and thought that it was typical Croatian propaganda; is that right?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Was my belief at the time, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And at a later stage, you realized that that information was in fact accurate?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct too.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Then you testified a little later in answer to the Presiding Judge's question about the timing and you said: "By early afternoon" - and that was the first day of the attack, the 4th - "we are finding that Knin is no longer our capital city." Now, at that time, were you referring to what you saw on TV which was not -- which did you not believe, or the confirmed information that you received later?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is really both. By the time I saw the film by HRTV, which was a Croatian radio television, soon after, the reports were started coming in from the people that were actually there, those who were pulling out, then Knin is history.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: I'm sorry. You just testified earlier that you did not have any communication with anyone from Sector South after the attack started.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't. By communication I mean being on a phone, being on a radio, being on a telex machine. These are the people who are actually going through Topusko telling us. They're not soldiers; they are civilians who are leaving the sectors.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And how did -- do you know how these people found out that Knin had fallen?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I didn't ask. I still considered this to be a rumour.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Okay. But you received that information in the afternoon of the first day of the operation?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, just for the witness' benefit, I think the exchange actually goes a little bit deeper, and he --

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: I think I'm entitled to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You're entitled to accurately summarize what was said, and if there's any dispute about that, then it is usually preferred to take the literal text so as to avoid whatever confusion.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Well, I was quoting from transcript reference 17953 at lines 18 and following, where it says: "By early afternoon," and it was established the lines above it, that is the first day of the operation. "We are finding out that Knin is no longer our capital city." And then I was trying to clarify that with the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, I'm looking at 17954 where in questioning with you, the witness said he wasn't -- he said, "It was either very late that night or very early in the morning. The night of the 4th." And then you, Mr. President, said, "Or early in the morning of the 5th." And the witness said, "5th, yes, thank you."

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And then I was trying to draw the distinction with what he saw on television and what was confirmed, and that was my next question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Well, the witness has now at least heard all of what was said, so to ask him to repeat doesn't make much sense. Mr. Hedaraly, if you have further questions on the matter, the witness is certainly now provided with the whole of his testimony yesterday. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Can you clarify for us the early afternoon, the early evening, the next morning, the unconfirmed, the TV report, the confirmed information later? Can you help us at all to sort this out?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I ask that the question be rephrased. I'm not sure what the question is.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: I think the witness understood the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lazarevic, if it is clear to you what Mr. Hedaraly would like to know, please answer the question. If it is unclear --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Absolutely, it is clear to me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It is clear to you. Then let's hear your answer. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The only thing I really claim right now, a little bit of confusion at the time, which is not surprising considering the situation that we were under. I'll try to sort it out chronologically. First, we saw the information on the TV. Later in the day, the trickle of people started coming into Topusko saying that Knin has fallen. Full confirmation of it is the following morning, early hours of the morning, because suddenly there are more people coming from south. That's about how it happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And this, the first step the TV and the people coming, that's the first day of the operation?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was late afternoon on first day.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Thank you. Now let's move a few days ahead, and you left the Krajina - that's in your statement on page 29 - on the 9th of August. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the morning, early hours of the morning when we left.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Do you remember it was the 9th of August?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would say, yes, 9th.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: That's the date in your statement. But it's around [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... It's 9th, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And did you have any knowledge at that time about the convoy of civilians leaving the southern portion of Sector South?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I think I made it perfectly clear that from day one we did not have any communication even with the clothes -- or corps, which were only -- like, our left flank, ten miles away; and our right flank, another ten miles away. So we had no idea what was going on down there. All we knew at the time was that we are surrounded.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: So you did not know anything about when, how, or why they were leaving?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Whom?

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: The people from Sector South.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, apparently they leaving in front of incoming Croatian forces. That's how I saw the thing. That's what I believed, anyway.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: But at the time you didn't have any of that information as to who was leaving, why they were leave, when they were leaving?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Not precise information. Nobody came to me and said, Look, I'm from Marshal Tito Street in Knin and I just left because Knin has fallen, and stuff like that, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: So what is described in your statement about the refugee convoy and what happened on the way, that's all what happened to you from Sector North leaving, right?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They were earlier convoys who left the Sector North going further south, straight into Bosnia. Along the border with the Bosnia and they were under constant attack by the 5th Corps. That would happen a second day of the attack, so when we came to decision to surrender and try to arrange for us leave as peaceful as possible, we decided to walk -- to go through Croatia, because we were absolutely certain that any agreement we made with the Croatians would not be honoured by the 5th Corps because they are not part of this agreement.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And you arrived in Belgrade the next day, on the 10th, right?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And that's when you saw the exits in the town blocked off by the police and people told to go south?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah. The reason why I went south is my wife's family lives approximately 200 kilometres south from Belgrade. So that is a normal route I would have taken anyway. It just happened to be the same one that all the convoys are going through and being prevented from leaving.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And this is all what you saw on the 10th of August?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Now, you don't know when this exits were blocked off, right?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can only assume it happened the day that we crossed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: So you have no information as to whether they were blocked off before the 10th, when you saw them?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Are you aware that most of the civilians from Dalmatia and Gracac and Lika left on the 4th and the 5th of August?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did find out later on. But at the time, no, I wasn't aware.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And are you aware that there were a number of witnesses who left these areas who testified in this case that they went to Belgrade, after Operation Storm?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Possible. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Do you know that there was a witness, and that is Witness 6, this Chamber's information, who testified at P16, paragraph 23, that he arrived Belgrade in the afternoon of the 5th and has been living there ever since?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Did you know that there was no mention in his testimony of being forced to go down to Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Do you know there's another witness, Dusan Sinobad, who him arrived in Belgrade on the 6th, after spending a night in Banja Luka, and similarly he never said anything about being forced to go to Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I'm saying is what happened on the 10th when I was going through. What happened before, I have no idea.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: I understand. I won't go through each of the witnesses who testified who now lives in Belgrade because obviously you're not aware of that information.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: If I can have 65 ter 7248 on the screen, please. The first page will be a cover page of a letter that we received from the Government of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Apparently there's a problem to get it on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, if we can get the other translation, please. We will get to this in a second. There are two different translations for different portions of this document. Actually, let's just stay there.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Okay. Now that we have it, this is a letter we received from the Government of Serbia on data regarding the people from the Krajina who are now registered in -- their residence registered in Serbia. It says that the data is incomplete because of the short-comings in the record-keeping method. So bear in mind this is an incomplete information.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: If we can go back to the other translation. Now, just, Mr. President, so that everyone is aware, the original is actually 600 and some pages and just lists everyone from 1 to 23595. We obviously did not translate each of the entries, because -- the total number was the concern. Similarly when we tender it, only the first and the last page can be -- can be tendered.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Mr. Lazarevic, my question for you is were aware that at least 23595 people who fled the Krajina after Storm had registered their residence in Serbia?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I was not aware. Actually, I'm surprised looking at the number it says 23595, and it is dated 7th. 7th of August?

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: No, no, no. That's from 2007.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, okay. Sorry, my bad.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: No problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: If we can go to the original in B/C/S, please. And think there is a technical issue in having both the B/C/S and the English on the screen at the same time, so we'll just work one at a time.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Now if we go to the second page of the B/C/S there. And this is -- and the cover letter also includes this information, and I will read it, but the translation is available. That these are people who, as of 2007, were registered in refugee camps in Serbia from the municipalities of Knin, Benkovac, Donji Lapac, Gracac, Drnis, and Obrovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: If we can go to the second page.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And we see the second portion is people from those areas who are in refugee centres in Kosovo. Now, the total is 779. I've counted it, and the people in refugee centres in Serbia total 725, and the ones in Kosovo total 54. Were you aware of that, Mr. Lazarevic?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It appeared to be a much larger number to me when I was driving through it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: This is as of 2007. But still -- people still live in those refugee camps in 2007, not in 1995.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh. I was not aware of that, no. But I'm seeing this, some of these refugee centres are away from Belgrade, further south.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Mm-hm. I understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: So if I can tender this document, and I propose only tendering the cover letter, these two pages, and then the first and last page of the B/C/S, of the large 600-page documents, and then the translations of the top lines on the first and last entries. And that is already uploaded as 65 ter 7248A.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any objections? Not only against the document but also the way in which they are presented? No objections. Just for my information, Mr. Hedaraly, when we started with this document, I looked in e-court and then I had -- you said different translation of different portions, but apparently part of those e-court documents. So I now see that what is on the e-court screen corresponds with your abbreviated version, which is with the total of 779, whereas the earlier ones with the As, et cetera, is --

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Those are two separate documents that were attached to the same cover letter. There was this two page documents about collection centres, then there was a separate 600-and-some-page document which is the people who registered their residence in Serbia. So those are two separate tables.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Two separate tables. And you're now tendering the cover letter?

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: The cover letter, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: The first table about the collection centres, the two pages.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And then the last --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Two pages, the first ...

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: The first saying: collection centres in -- if we go back to the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Because what we see now on our screen, Abu Asad, Acimovic, that apparently is -- is that something you want to tender?

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Yes. If we can pull up 65 ter 7248A.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But that's a different document?

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: It's the same document. There -- there are three documents in the same exhibit. There's the cover page, the cover letter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Then there is the two-page document about collection centres.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And then in the original, there is 600-page table with 23.000 entries. Now what I'm proposing to tender, and not to tender 600 pages, is simply the first three pages, the cover letter and the two pages about the collection centres. And only the first and last page of the 600-page table so that we can see the first and last number. And that is uploaded in the 65 ter number I have mentioned 7248A.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I now see it. The original is 686 pages, including the cover letter. The translation is split up in two parts, both dealing only with a limited portion of the original; one portion, 1 to 3 and then interrupted, and then finally ending at 23595; that is the persons registered. And then the other portion of the translation about the, as it said, collective centres.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: In translation, one page, going from number 1 to 41; and then collective centres, Kosovo and Metohija, 42 up till 51, total of 779 persons those centres.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Yes. And I apologise for not having clarified that earlier, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, it's clear to me now. So that this all together is one exhibit, and there are no objections. Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that becomes Exhibit P2534.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Mr. Lazarevic, I apologise for the little procedural delay we have now and again. Now, before Operation Storm, would you communicate with your counterpart, the liaison officer for Sector South on a regular basis?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not really. You're talking about the RSK?

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For example, the liaison officer of Sector South?

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Only if somebody happened, they would either influence the situation down south or would affect Sector North, then we would get in touch.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: For example, when you received the plans of attack, then you communicated with them.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: I want to talk a little bit about the recruitment of interpreters about which you testified. Now this idea of using interpreters to gain information from internationals, whose idea was that?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would like to think it was mine, but I might be wrong.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Well, was it your idea or -- what did you mean by you'd like to think that it was yours?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I implemented it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Okay. And you also testified yesterday that it was not limited to interpreters but any person -- any local employed in the -- in the workforce, with the internationals?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Any potential employee, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Now you testified yesterday that your belief was that the same thing happened in Sector South, but you don't have any actual knowledge of that. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And you be the person giving them instructions to these interpreters and cleaners or dishwashers, as you called them?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the interpreters, yes, myself personally.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: What about to the other people that were employed? Would you instruct them as wall as to what to do?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that would be done by the members of the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Okay. And what would you tell these interpreters? What were your instructions to them?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My instructions were very simple. Basically, since we are covering a fairly large territory, there will be meetings on a daily basis, whether it is Slunj, whether it's in Vojnic, whether it's Vrginmost, which were of the, let's say, lesser importance meetings, local character, things concerning only Topusko, for example, or things concerning only Vrginmost. And those interpreters would attend those meetings without me being present there. I would ask them to, at the end of the meeting, prepare me the list of the people attending the meeting, from all sides, the minutes of the meeting, and the brief description, if anything was decided on a meeting, what it was. And to submit it to me the very same evening.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Did you instruct them to steal documents or take photographs or anything like that?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No. These people were not professional in -- in spying business, if you like.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Did you instruct them to try and falsify the reports that internationals were sending?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely not.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Did you instruct them to talk to internationals and get them to change their reports?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think any of those people were aware of the reports were being sent by the internationals to influence them in any way.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: So if I understood you correctly, their job was not to affect the reporting but, rather, to tell you what was happening; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Now, let's talk briefly about this ECMM monitor, Bent Jenssen you said in your statement that he showed you some of the reports that he was sending; is that right?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Would he show them to you on a regular basis or was it just a -- once in a while or occasional?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It wasn't a regular basis. It was not like he was reporting to me daily what he was sending. But every now and then if something did happen in the area that was of some relevance, he would come into his office and, This is what I'm going to send. I read it, without any suggestions, and he says, So are you going to change this, or I like the way you wrote it, it was just accepted by me as such.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: So you never told him what to write?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely not.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Did you know any of the ECMM monitors that were in Sector South in 1995?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Unless they were first in Sector North and then moved down there. But I had never contacted anybody from south.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Did you know any of the UNMOs that were in Sector South in 1995?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, the same thing. If they were originally deployed along the border where I was, of course, I would know them. And if they transferred down south, then I can say, Yes, I know this guy. Otherwise, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And would the same be true as members of UNCIVPOL, of HRAT, or any other international organisation?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Exactly the same position.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Now, you testified yesterday, and I'll quote you exactly at transcript page 17956, lines 1 to 4: "Q. Did you sense any increased concern about a pending Croatian attack? "A. Nobody knew about the attack two days before it happened. I found out two days before it happened." Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Now, in the Milosevic trial, which was also tendered here at 12452, you said the same thing, that Mr. Jenssen informed you about the attack two days before. But you also stated that those plans contained, and I'll quote, "every detail about the time, the strength, and the direction of attack." Just pause for the translation.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, that is correct. But I think I also clarified he did not give me a document. It was narrated to me, and I wrote it down.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Now, I just wanted to clarify in the Milosevic trial at that page, you said that the attack started on the 5th, but just to so you know, I think the parties are in agreement that Operation Storm actually started on the 4th August, so that could have just been a mistake.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My omission. Because all I remembered was early in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Can you please tell us what you mean by every detail of the attack that you received?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let us assume just for a moment that I'm in a conflict with another country. To me a detailed information would be the time, I know where they're going to attack, the strength of the enemy attack. So if you tell me that 20.000 people fronting you, that is very important to me. The direction of the attack is also very important. They are going come from the direction of Karlovac, for example, heading for Tusilovic. I would say, yes, that is very important. To me, that is a detailed enough. You know whether there going to be consistent of the 1st Guards Brigade, and this and that, to me, is irrelevant. I know the number is going to be 20.000, I know they're going to come from this way, I better do something about it. That's what I mean detailed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: So did you have information about which units would attack where?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Just the time, the direction, and the strength?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Okay. And you just said that this is oral information that he brought to you two days before the attack?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: So he did not have any documents with him. He just came to you and said he had memorized this information and was saying it to you?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Basically this is what I remember, this is what is going to happen.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Now, these plans that he gave you orally, did they include any detail about the attack on Sector South?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely no.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Did you have any information about the attack on Sector South, it's time, strength, or direction?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, no. The information he gave us to led to us believe that the Croatian forces are going to join with the 5th corps behind us, and that we're going to get caught in a pincher. So that, for us, was very, very, important.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And now you're talking about Sector North, right?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: So you had no information whatsoever about the attack on Sector South?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: None whatsoever. I know it is shortcoming from direction of Petrinja, so Banja Corps had to know about it. And I know it is coming from a direction of Karlovac, which is important to us because it is it our own AOR. So those two directions they were coming, yes, that was very important.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: You also testified about the fear that the Serbs in the Krajina had about the Croatian forces. Do you remember testifying about that?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, on several occasions.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And you have also testified that the Croatian army helped creating the fear by situations like Medak pocket, Maslenica, and other operations?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And yesterday while discussing this flag over Knin castle, you referred to Croatian propaganda. Would such propaganda also instill fear in the Serbs in Sector North?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely. The radio waves were open completely between us and them. You can listen to radio Osijek if you wanted to or radio Zagreb while you're in RSK. So whatever is happening over there, we can be fed with all sorts of things without being absolutely certain this is what is happening.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And did you hear any -- any public statements made by Croatians that reinforced those fears?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Myself personally, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Did you hear of any such public statements being made by Croatians?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Now it's totally now fuzzy in my head. Whether I heard it or somebody told me about it, the late president Tudjman said it was Krajina without Serbs in it. That was not a secret; everybody knew that. But I can't claim today 20 years ago whether I heard that on the TV, whether I heard it from somebody who was present, I can't really say. But that would be one of the things to me, very important.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Are you familiar with the Spegelj tapes?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Done by the JNA or any other tapes?

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Well, the tapes that --

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Tapes which I know about are done by the JNA, and that was before it's conflict.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Okay. I'm referring to tapes done during the conflict.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The ones which they screened on a local TV was the plan of what the Croatian army is going do, or what is expected from them. And it's recorded every JNA officer and kill him on the spot in the place where they live, for example.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, if we can get some foundation on what tape during the conflict Mr. Hedaraly is referring to. I'm not aware of any such tape.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hedaraly, is this a suggestion you're willing follow or ...

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: I would prefer not. I mean, we can ask the witness what he just described what that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, if he perhaps would explain to us about these tapes what they are, because that's not ...

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Just so we're clear, Mr. President, the witness testified about JNA tapes before the conflict which we will concede the point existed. If we're going into some other tapes involving Mr. Spegelj during the conflict, then I think counsel has an obligation to have a good faith basis to say that such tapes existed. Because I'm just saying I'm unaware of it, and if he can help me out and tell me what that is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hedaraly, as guidance from the Chamber, you are invited to follow the suggestion of Mr. Misetic, primarily because matters are not perfectly clear to the Chamber, at least not to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: I can just ask the witness, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: What you testified to that you heard about what was going to happen, when did you hear that? You said it was screened on TV. Can you give information as to what that was, that you saw --

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You got me confused. Are we still talking about the Spegelj tapes?

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Spegelj tapes were screened fairly regularly. Anytime they wanted to create a bit of a panic and say, Well, this is what we're going expect from them. This is it. These tapes are made prior to conflict, you're correct. So I have not seen any tapes made after the actual conflict has started.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And they were not made, but were they played during the conflict?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were played, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And they said that the Croatian authorities would slaughter the Serbs in Knin, that it would kill the officers of the JNA, their wives, and that this would be a general slaughter house. Is that the general --

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Basically that was the idea of the tapes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: So the reality is that there was propaganda and fear on both sides and fostered by both sides; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm going to object. The witness needs to be asked - I think he indicated it, but to the extent it was unclear - who was playing the Spegelj tapes and for what purpose.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I think the witness indicated who was playing the tapes. So he can't say both sides unless he has established --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Unless we're not just talking about these tapes, but talking about a wider propaganda machine on both sides. That's at least what I understood.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please specify in your question exactly, if you say both sides and propaganda, what the kind of propaganda exactly was, so as to say that they were broadcast by this and by this party, with similar content of things to be expected or different content, so that we get more than just a yes or no on a question which is lacking sufficient precision.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Mr. Lazarevic, are you aware of any propaganda by the Croatian side about what would happen to the Serbs in the Krajina?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: During the time of the conflict?

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. You have to realize for the first year and a half we had no power; we had no electricity. I was living by a tiny little bulb like that that was connected to the battery of my car. So we had no possibility of watching TV or listening to the radio or reading the daily news or anything like that, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And you testified yesterday that that fear was also created or, at least, entertained, in part, by the actions of the Croatian forces in other military operations. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. And I add, I'll give you a perfect example when they are screening Croatian parliament, there's going to be a gentleman come up on the stage and he goes with the -- he raises his right fist and says "za dom spremni." If you are a Serb, it makes you feel very uneasy.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Can you just please say what you mean "za dom spremni" in English, just for the transcript?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You can't even try to translate that. It's "za dom spremni," ready for the homeland. That would be as close as I can come. But it was a typical salute of the Ustashas during the World War II.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And is that why it would make Serbs feel uneasy?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely. My own side, if they wanted to increase a bit of attention and say, Well, we can't live with them, they would just refer to 1945 -- back to 1945. This is what happened to you then. What do you expect from them today? And they would come up with a little video of, you know, of filming the areas which were recently under attack by the Croatian forces, like Medak pocket, scorched earth, everything is dead, chicken, pigs, people, nothing is moving.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And was that, as far as you are aware, are these things that actually happened, or were they just made up by the RSK?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. They did happen. There's sufficient evidence of things that happened in -- in Maslenica by the international community reported. There's sufficient documentation supported -- gathered by the Canadian army which was in -- in area of Medak pocket at the time. That's film footage, there are documents, statements.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And all of these contributed to the fear that the Serbs had of the Croatian forces?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Reinforced fear, I can say. Not create something new.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Mm-hm.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All you had to is just light up a little fire under something that is already there, lurking in a corner somewhere. So just do a little -- emphasise it a bit and then bring it back to life again.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Mr. President, now would be a good time for a break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It is a good time for a break. We will resume at ten minutes past 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Just very briefly, I do understand that the portion of the video that was played and which has received D1469, has now been uploaded in e-court. Mr. Registrar, you would not contradict the Defence in this respect, would you? No? You're nodding no. That means that D1469 is admitted into evidence. Any further progress in relation to the evidence, in relation to possible videolink? I think you would --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: My apologies, Your Honour, that fell off the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Fell off the agenda.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, your agendas during the breaks are most likely as busy as ours are. Okay. No news there. Next break?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And may -- I was reminded that I failed to do something yesterday. We used the organigram with the witness yesterday, and failed to tender it. So if Mr. Hedaraly wouldn't mind if I could just tender this. It's 65 ter 1D2685.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: I don't mind if Mr. Misetic tenders it now. And I will not object to it either.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, that would be?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1470, Your Honours.
